claims.claim_text: On prime_gap, the certified learned rule gate improves top-1 over both the raw scorer and the hand-wheel gate while preserving zero false rejections.
claims.summary: learned gate 68.87% vs hand-wheel 45.12% vs raw 9.13%; false rejections=0.
claims.title: Prime learned gate improves top-1 over raw and hand-wheel gates

claims.claim_text: On prime_gap, the neural rule proposer is useful at fixed verifier budget relative to grammar-order and structural baselines.

contradicted_if: neural_structural trails grammar_order and structural_heuristic on any reported grammar

residual: Treat the current Axis 2 row as a negative or mixed result, not a proposer-usefulness proof.
Run R-E2.1 for 5+ seeds and budget grids.
Run R-E2.2/R-E2.3 only if the richer grammar creates non-saturated cases where learned ordering can matter.
claims.summary: static neural proposer trails deterministic baselines on at least one grammar; candidate static=72.49 saved vs grammar=73.22, conditional static=2.15 saved vs grammar=55.57.
claims.title: Prime neural proposer beats fixed-budget symbolic baselines

claims.claim_text: When trained on the fixed ARC task but evaluated on held-out same-envelope ARC variants, the shared multitask scorer beats the single-task ARC scorer.
claims.paper_explanation: This supports the narrow residual-generalization claim: the shared scorer loses on the fixed ARC training task, but improves held-out same-envelope ARC ranking and log loss.
claims.summary: shared OOD top-1 48.40% vs single 42.83% (+5.57pp), NLL 2.6278 vs 4.3723.
claims.title: Shared scorer beats single-task scorer on same-envelope ARC OOD

claims.claim_text: The public ARC certified transform gate and budgeted proposer measurements are unchanged under shared-scorer and single-task-scorer context labels in the current implementation.
claims.paper_explanation: This separates the certified ARC gate from learned scorer choice: the public ARC gate/proposer measurements are currently scorer-independent, so scorer claims and gate claims remain cleanly separated.
claims.summary: ARC gate/proposer invariance holds across scorer-context labels: train 24/400 certified tasks, eval 4/400, mismatches=0.
claims.title: Public ARC certified gate is invariant to scorer context labels

claims.claim_text: The paper reports public ARC train/eval certified-task and covered-cell counts as a measured evidence surface rather than as a broad ARC-performance claim.

supported_if: latest measured evaluation certified_tasks >= v12_recorded evaluation certified_tasks
latest measured evaluation test_correct_cells >= v12_recorded evaluation test_correct_cells

claims.paper_explanation: This is not a broad ARC-performance claim. It is the public-corpus parity row: the compiler can now distinguish measured ARC gate coverage, version-to-version movement, and the much larger unresolved residual.
claims.summary: public ARC evidence surface improves from v10 eval 4 tasks/187 cells to v15_measured eval 7 tasks/1057 cells; v15_measured train remains 24 tasks/1187 cells.
claims.title: Public ARC corpus parity row is measured and scoped

claims.claim_text: On ARC, the shared scorer improves log loss but worsens fixed-task ECE, while improving both log loss and ECE on same-envelope OOD evaluation.
claims.paper_explanation: The calibration claim is explicitly conditional: shared training is not simply better calibrated everywhere. It is worse on fixed ARC ECE but better on OOD ECE, while improving log loss in both settings.
claims.summary: ARC shared scorer is a calibration tradeoff: fixed-task NLL improves (4.0827 vs 8.2754) while ECE worsens (0.6995 vs 0.5589); OOD improves both NLL (2.6278 vs 4.3723) and ECE (0.4481 vs 0.4820).
claims.title: ARC shared scorer has a fixed-task versus OOD calibration tradeoff

claims.claim_text: Delayed_claim benefits from shared training at matched updates, but the sibling effect is specific rather than universal.
claims.paper_explanation: This replaces the earlier broad positive-transfer claim with a narrower one: delayed_claim benefits from shared training in this envelope, grid_path appears to be the helpful sibling, and ARC is mild interference.
claims.summary: delayed_claim all-domain top-1 98.00% vs claim-only 96.60% (+1.40pp); removing grid_path falls to 97.20%, while removing ARC rises to 98.50%.
claims.title: Delayed-claim transfer gain is sibling-specific

claims.claim_text: A four-capacity sweep changes the fixed ARC shared-vs-single gap but does not monotonically close it, while delayed_claim remains non-negative across capacities.

supported_if: all ARC capacity rows have seeds >= 3
ARC delta is not monotone non-decreasing with parameter count

claims.paper_explanation: This keeps the architecture roadmap disciplined: capacity changes the ARC gap, but does not monotonically close it, so adapters or ordering should not be claimed until the tiny-net plateau check is done.
claims.summary: capacity sweep rules out a simple wider-is-better ARC story: best fixed-ARC shared row is 32x16 at 39.20%, but every shared ARC row trails single-task; delayed_claim deltas remain +0.10pp to +0.43pp.
claims.title: Capacity sweep does not explain away the ARC fixed-task gap

claims.claim_text: Verifier rejection reasons can be fed back into the proposer so that reason-aware and trained-residual ranking avoid unsafe rows and improve budgeted validation utility on the prime/modular gate family.

supported_if: model_score picks unsafe rows and produces validation false rejections at budget 8
reason_prior and trained_residual have zero unsafe rows and zero validation false rejections at budget 8
prime_gap and modular_gate split sweeps have zero trained_residual validation false rejections and nonnegative utility deltas

claims.paper_explanation: This is the first substrate-level self-authoring loop: rejected verifier rows are converted into reasons, then those reasons improve the next proposer pass. The claim is scoped to the prime/modular sweeps; delayed_claim remains a stress case. Seed-interval and reason-family artifacts are reported when present so the paper can distinguish stable proposer repair from a single favorable trace.
claims.summary: reason learning repairs the prime proposer failure at budget 8: model_score selects 7 unsafe rows and causes 172 validation false rejections, while reason_prior reaches 6 accepted rules/216.0 utility and trained_residual reaches 7 accepted rules/245.0 utility with zero false rejections; prime/modular split sweeps pass, but delayed_claim has 0 mixed split rows.
claims.title: Rejected-candidate reasons repair proposer ranking on prime/modular gates

claims.claim_text: Zero-false-rejection hypothesis promotions can be reused as slot priors that improve learned proposal coverage and utility in the ARC hypothesis fixture.

supported_if: at least one promoted library row has support_tasks >= 2 and false_rejections == 0
slot_prior learned certified@1 > no_prior learned certified@1
slot_prior learned utility@8 > no_prior learned utility@8
both compared learned rows preserve zero false rejections

claims.paper_explanation: This makes the hypothesis library a generated claim rather than a roadmap note. Fixture feedback and held-out feedback are separated in machine-readable rows; public ARC promotion remains the R-S.1c gap before using it as a headline ARC claim.
claims.summary: certified-library promotion supports fixture-level feedback: promoted move_to_anchor from 2 tasks/78 covered events with zero false rejections; slot priors raise learned certified@1 from 2 to 4 and utility@8 from 0.2119 to 0.5169. Held-out split feedback rows: 30.
claims.title: Certified hypothesis libraries feed back into proposal ranking

claims.claim_text: Before increasing neural capacity, the paper reports a same-ladder tiny-net audit with learning curves, restart variance, best checkpoint, plateau detection, parameter count, FLOPs, and width-help verdicts for each core task.

supported_if: all core domains have the same four-capacity shared tiny-net ladder
every shared row has plateau_detected == true
width-help rows exist for each core domain

claims.paper_explanation: This turns the width discussion into an audit: the paper can distinguish undertraining from representation limits using learning curves, restarts, best checkpoints, parameter counts, FLOPs, plateau flags, and width-help rows.
residual: Do not explain ARC or learned-wheel failures as capacity limits until this audit is present.
Run make tiny-net-plateau-audit and inspect the width-help verdicts before increasing default hidden sizes.
claims.summary: tiny-net plateau audit covers 4 capacities across 4 domains; 10/16 shared rows meet the plateau threshold, and ARC shared width verdict picks 16x8 as best hidden.
claims.title: Tiny-net architecture claims are gated by plateau audits

claims.claim_text: The prime trace replay contract is deterministic at the semantic layer: float and double runs produce the same replay-semantic trace hash while reporting FP-sensitive rank rows explicitly.

supported_if: every audit row reports rank_fp_sensitive_rate and semantic_hash

claims.paper_explanation: The reproducibility claim is semantic rather than bit-exact: float and double runs may differ in logits and calibration diagnostics, but the replay-semantic trace projection has the same hash and exposes every rank-sensitive row.
claims.summary: trace determinism audit covers 2 traces and 2000 rows; invalid_rows=0, rank_fp_sensitive_rows=0, logged_mismatches=0, semantic_hashes_equal=True.
claims.title: Trace replay semantics are deterministic across float and double runs

claims.claim_text: On held-out replay-certified Signal flight groups, a tiny WASD ranker improves top-1, utility, and regret against the primitive no-safety goal-heading baseline without increasing measured damage or death rate.

supported_if: neural regret is lower than baseline_regret
neural damage and death rates are no worse than baseline on the held-out trace

claims.paper_explanation: This is an application vignette, not a live-control claim: Signal contributes a replay-certified bounded-control surface where the neural component ranks nine WASD candidates and simulator replay owns the outcome labels.
claims.summary: Signal offline replay ranker top-1 79.76% vs baseline 67.86% (+11.90pp), utility 0.1432 vs 0.1359, regret 0.0073 vs 0.0146, damage 2.38% vs 2.38%, deaths 0.00% vs 0.00%; live shadow frames=22191.
claims.title: Signal replay-certified WASD ranker improves held-out control utility

claims.claim_text: A guarded Signal neural_active live pilot executes checkpoint-ranked WASD actions on a running local server with logged active-source, checkpoint hash, inference latency, safety gates, damage/death telemetry, and replay-ready trace rows.
claims.paper_explanation: This supports only the existence of guarded live neural-active execution: the running Signal pilot applies checkpoint-ranked WASD actions and logs the fields needed for replay. It does not yet show that active neural control improves utility or safety versus the heuristic baseline.
claims.summary: Signal live neural-active pilot executed 250 recent neural-source rows from checkpoint f12b644ed9fa with p95 inference 0.124 ms, 249 replay-ready rows, safety-gate rows=250, damage events=0, deaths=0; no baseline comparison is claimed.
claims.title: Signal guarded neural-active pilot executes live checkpoint-ranked actions
